notes.note: Checked Stable and Nightly scope admission against the manifest and runtime sweep. Each admitted scope is listed and ledger-triaged before fair delete rounds, within the same call and delete ceilings. The synthetic Apple fixture demonstrates progress with sustained demand; Apple quotas and deployed admission remain separate.

Checked the notification record timer/expiry owner, Web Push paused/replaced registrations and APNs sweep. Controlled paths verify generation ownership, persistence-before-exposure, long deadlines and fair delete opportunities. Deployment and live device delivery are outside these receipts.

Traced the authenticated discovery response and exact browser/Station fingerprint match through the SDK, App authority scope, hook and Settings. HTTP and persistence fixtures cover delayed gone, replacement and same-endpoint refresh; Chromium exercises distinct discovery refusals. Physical push delivery stays separately qualified.

Checked the public discovery export and transport request options through the real client wire parser. The VAPID read retains HTTP status and the paired-device response contains an opaque fingerprint. The timer information describes service-owned persisted deadlines rather than a transport promise.

Checked notification lifecycle types against the persisted scheduler and expiry paths. A bounded timer rechecks its own revision and deadline, and delivering does not imply downstream display. The native timer and controlled-clock tests establish the claimed behavior.

Checked the browser Web Push description against the selected Station scope, actual Settings status component and App-level default reset. Disabling revokes the local subscription. A remote cleanup failure is visible and remains distinct from the local outcome.
